reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, post-fix stale re-review batch 0, 2026-08-02

samples_reviewed.question_text: Maria wakes up at 11:00. What time is that?
Jose leaves for school at 1:00. What time is that?
A class survey showed 10 students like costume sash and 1 student like wristband. How many students were surveyed in all?
Maria starts homework at 2:00. What time is that?
Jose solved this problem: "A class survey showed 10 students like fan shirt and 3 students like tote bag. How many students were surveyed in all?" Jose says the answer is 13. Is Jose correct?
A class survey showed 3 students like marker set and 15 students like tarpaulin print. How many students were surveyed in all? The answer is 18.. True or False?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Three of eight samples are student-survey addition problems with no time content at all: seed 44's 'A class survey showed 10 students like costume sash and 1 student like wristband,' seed 50's Jose check on a fan-shirt/tote-bag survey, and seed 110's marker-set/tarpaulin-print survey -- none involves an hour, day, or month.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency names hour, half hour, quarter hour, days in a week, and months in a year, but every clock sample (seeds 42, 43, 46) shows only a whole hour like '11:00' or '2:00'; half hour, quarter hour, days of the week, and months of the year never appear anywhere in the eight samples.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Seed 51's 'Set the clock to show 4:00' is an appropriately concrete Grade 1 task, but the off-topic seed 44's survey wording, 'A class survey showed 10 students like costume sash and 1 student like wristband,' introduces retail vocabulary ('costume sash', 'wristband') unrelated to any time concept this node is meant to teach.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Direct time-reading (seeds 42, 43, 46) and clock-setting (seed 51) variants exist, but the 'problem-solving' framing that does appear, seeds 44, 50, and 110, is a student-merchandise survey count entirely unrelated to time, so no elapsed-time or calendar word problem is ever produced.

competency_alignment.rationale: The three survey samples vary student counts and item names, e.g. seed 110's 'marker set' versus 'tarpaulin print' totaling 18, an axis that has nothing to do with 'problems involving time'; even the on-topic samples never progress beyond restating a stated whole-hour time.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The time samples stay within a simple 1:00-11:00 whole-hour range fit for Grade 1, e.g. seed 42's 11:00, but the survey items introduce unrelated totals up to 18 (seed 110) that map to no hour, day, or month scale this node is supposed to teach.
